review_status: Draft instrument — AWS expert validation required

review_metadata.notes: Derived implementation of capstone scope. The PDF provides a proposed instrument, not a finalized expert-approved rule matrix. All service rules, question phrasing, framework mappings, and sources require qualified AWS expert review.

questions.text: Will the website store or serve files, images, or other objects?
questions.help: Select Yes for durable object storage requirements such as images, documents, and downloadable assets.

questions.text: Will the website serve static HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or media assets?
questions.help: A static asset requirement can select Amazon S3; a private origin with CloudFront is generally preferable to exposing a bucket.

questions.text: Will users upload files or objects through the website?
questions.help: Select Yes when authenticated uploads need object storage and narrowly scoped upload authorization.

questions.text: Are least-privilege roles and restricted bucket or access point policies planned?
questions.help: Confirm who can read, write, list, or change S3 access; avoid broad principals and long-lived shared credentials.

questions.text: Will public bucket access be blocked and object delivery use a deliberately controlled path?
questions.help: For public website assets, a private S3 origin with CloudFront Origin Access Control can provide a controlled public delivery path.

questions.text: Will object classification, encryption, and protection of sensitive uploads be addressed?
questions.help: S3 automatically encrypts new uploads, but key policy, classification, transport security, and access boundaries still require review.

questions.text: Will appropriate S3 access activity and security-relevant changes be logged and reviewed?
questions.help: CloudTrail data events for object access are not enabled by default. Select coverage deliberately and account for logging costs.

questions.text: Will bucket settings, versioning, lifecycle rules, and public access defaults be reviewed?
questions.help: Confirm the intended storage design and test permissions before deployment; select retention and recovery settings deliberately.

questions.text: Does the application require relational tables or SQL queries?
questions.help: Select Yes for a relational data model or relational SQL requirement. Transactions alone do not distinguish RDS from DynamoDB, which also supports transactions.

questions.text: Does the application need a key-value or document data store with defined access patterns?
questions.help: Select Yes for a NoSQL data requirement that can fit DynamoDB. Both database choices can apply to different parts of a website.

questions.text: Are distinct, least-privilege database administrators and application identities planned?
questions.help: Use service-appropriate identities: database credentials or supported IAM authentication for RDS, and IAM authorization for DynamoDB.

questions.text: Will database network access be restricted to the intended applications?
questions.help: For RDS, avoid public accessibility and broad ingress. For DynamoDB, review endpoint policies and the need for VPC endpoints.

questions.text: Are encryption, secure client connections, and data recovery protections planned?
questions.help: Confirm database-specific encryption and key access, TLS connections, backups, and tested restoration against stated needs.

questions.text: Will database administrative activity, access indicators, and failures be logged and reviewed?
questions.help: Choose appropriate service logs and CloudTrail event coverage; logging requirements vary between RDS and DynamoDB.

questions.text: Will the database model, access patterns, backup settings, and capacity configuration be reviewed?
questions.help: Validate relational versus NoSQL suitability; different data stores may both be needed for different application components.

questions.text: Does the application require control of a server operating system or VM?
questions.help: Select Yes for custom OS packages, persistent server processes, or a workload requiring a virtual machine.

questions.text: Can the application run as event-driven functions within Lambda limits?
questions.help: Select Yes for request or event handlers suited to AWS Lambda. Confirm current duration, memory, packaging, and integration limits.

questions.text: Will the application run continuously or require jobs beyond Lambda execution limits?
questions.help: Select Yes for a long-running workload requiring EC2 among the covered services. Capacity and resilience require additional design.

questions.text: Will compute use narrowly scoped execution roles rather than embedded access keys?
questions.help: Review EC2 instance profiles or Lambda execution roles and the permissions used by deployment automation.

questions.text: Will public exposure and compute network paths be explicitly restricted?
questions.help: Review EC2 security groups and subnet placement; for Lambda distinguish function invocation policies from VPC interface traffic.

questions.text: Will application secrets, storage encryption, and sensitive runtime data be protected?
questions.help: Avoid plaintext credentials in code or deployment files. Use a suitable secrets service and review encryption key permissions.

questions.text: Will application logs, infrastructure events, and failure alerts be configured and reviewed?
questions.help: Define useful log content and retention; avoid writing sensitive values or credentials into logs.

questions.text: Will runtime limits, secure defaults, patching responsibilities, and deployment settings be reviewed?
questions.help: For EC2 review images, updates, and metadata settings. For Lambda review runtime support, resource limits, and invocation permissions.

questions.text: Will you manage the website’s public domain and DNS records on AWS?
questions.help: Select Yes for Route 53 authoritative DNS management. An existing external DNS provider can remain in use when No is selected.

questions.text: Will the website use a content delivery network or a controlled public edge?
questions.help: Select Yes for CloudFront distribution, caching, HTTPS delivery, or a private S3 origin behind a public edge.

questions.text: Does the website need edge caching for visitors in multiple regions?
questions.help: Select Yes for a CloudFront global delivery requirement. This does not select multi-region compute or database deployment.

questions.text: Will DNS and distribution changes be limited to authorized administrators?
questions.help: Restrict permissions for Route 53 zones, DNS records, CloudFront distributions, and related certificate configuration.

questions.text: Will origins, DNS targets, and public delivery routes have defined exposure boundaries?
questions.help: Restrict direct origin access where possible and verify that DNS records target resources controlled by the organization.

questions.text: Will HTTPS and appropriate protection of sensitive cached or DNS-related data be planned?
questions.help: Enforce suitable viewer and origin TLS policies for CloudFront. Review DNSSEC for DNS integrity and avoid secrets in DNS records.

questions.text: Will DNS or edge activity and configuration changes have appropriate logging and review?
questions.help: Choose relevant query, access, and control-plane logs. Plan retention, access restrictions, and alerting for important changes.

questions.text: Will DNS records, cache behaviors, domain ownership, and retired targets be reviewed?
questions.help: Check record targets and aliases, cache keys, certificate region requirements, and removal of stale DNS after decommissioning.

questions.text: Will people or application workloads need identities or permissions for AWS resources?
questions.help: IAM is also included as a dependency whenever another covered AWS service is identified. Prefer federation and short-lived roles.

questions.text: Will you manage an HTTPS certificate for an AWS-supported endpoint?
questions.help: Select Yes for ACM certificate management on an integrated endpoint, such as a custom domain on CloudFront. ACM is not a general-purpose TLS proxy.

questions.text: Will a VPC-attached workload require a controlled inbound or outbound network boundary?
questions.help: Select Yes for Security Groups on EC2, RDS, or a VPC-attached Lambda interface. Lambda without VPC attachment does not automatically need a Security Group.

questions.text: Are federation or least-privilege identities, MFA for human access, and protected administrator credentials planned?
questions.help: Prefer short-lived credentials, protect the root user, and regularly review roles, trust policies, and any unavoidable access keys.

questions.text: Will security boundaries and trusted administrative or service access paths be restricted?
questions.help: Review security group sources and destinations and relevant IAM or certificate access paths. Avoid unnecessary administrative exposure.

questions.text: Will certificates, credentials, and encryption key access be protected?
questions.help: Use managed certificate renewal where supported, avoid embedding secrets, and restrict access to certificate material and credentials.

questions.text: Will security-relevant identity, certificate, and boundary changes be logged and reviewed?
questions.help: Enable appropriate CloudTrail coverage and consider alerts for privilege changes, certificate failures, and broad ingress changes.

questions.text: Will role policies, certificate lifecycle, and security group rules be reviewed before deployment?
questions.help: Validate IAM trust and permission policies, ACM validation and renewal prerequisites, and removal of unused security group rules.

s3.name: Amazon S3
s3.reason: Amazon S3 provides durable object storage for the stated static asset, file storage, or upload requirement.

risks.title: Excessive object or bucket permissions
risks.description: Broad IAM or bucket policies can allow unintended object reads, writes, deletion, or policy changes.
risks.action: Use least-privilege roles and bucket policies, restrict principals and prefixes, and review cross-account access.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Unintended public bucket exposure
risks.description: Public bucket or access point permissions can bypass the intended website delivery boundary.
risks.action: Enable S3 Block Public Access where applicable and use CloudFront Origin Access Control for a private S3 origin.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Inadequate data and key protection
risks.description: Default object encryption alone does not establish correct key permissions, data classification, or protection of sensitive uploads.
risks.action: Classify stored data, require secure transport, review encryption and key policy, and restrict sensitive object access.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Missing object access visibility
risks.description: Unselected object-level audit coverage can leave reads or writes unavailable for investigation.
risks.action: Select appropriate CloudTrail S3 data events, protect audit logs, and define review and retention procedures.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unreviewed bucket recovery and lifecycle settings
risks.description: Inappropriate versioning, lifecycle, or bucket settings can expose or unintentionally delete website data.
risks.action: Review public access defaults, enable appropriate versioning, and test lifecycle and recovery settings before deployment.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

rds.name: Amazon RDS
rds.reason: Amazon RDS fits the stated need for a managed relational database with relational tables or SQL queries.

risks.title: Overprivileged database identities
risks.description: Shared administrator credentials or broad IAM permissions can grant unnecessary database control.
risks.action: Use separate administrative and application identities, least-privilege grants, and supported IAM authentication where appropriate.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Publicly accessible database instance
risks.description: Public accessibility and broad security group ingress can expose the database to unintended clients.
risks.action: Use private subnets where appropriate, review Publicly accessible, and restrict security group ingress to intended application identities or sources.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unprotected database data or connections
risks.description: Unreviewed storage encryption, TLS requirements, or backup protection can expose database content.
risks.action: Enable appropriate RDS encryption, require supported TLS client connections, protect key access, and define tested backups.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Insufficient database audit trails
risks.description: Missing engine logs or administrative event coverage can prevent investigation of database misuse.
risks.action: Enable appropriate database logs and CloudTrail administrative coverage, review access indicators, and set retention.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unsuitable database or recovery settings
risks.description: An unreviewed engine, parameter group, backup, or capacity setting can undermine the stated relational workload.
risks.action: Validate engine and SQL requirements, review parameter groups and patch settings, and test backup restoration.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

dynamodb.name: Amazon DynamoDB
dynamodb.reason: Amazon DynamoDB fits the stated key-value or document data requirement with defined access patterns.

risks.title: Overbroad table and API permissions
risks.description: Wildcard DynamoDB permissions can expose table data or administrative operations beyond application needs.
risks.action: Restrict IAM actions and table or index resources, use workload roles, and consider fine-grained access conditions.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Unrestricted DynamoDB access paths
risks.description: An unrestricted endpoint or identity policy can permit table operations outside the intended network context.
risks.action: Review IAM conditions and endpoint policies; use a DynamoDB VPC endpoint when required by the access design.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unreviewed encryption and recovery protection
risks.description: Inappropriate key permissions, client security, or recovery settings can expose data or hinder restoration.
risks.action: Review encryption key ownership and permissions, require TLS, and enable point-in-time recovery when needed.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Missing table-level audit coverage
risks.description: Without appropriate CloudTrail event selection, table data activity may not be available for review.
risks.action: Configure the required DynamoDB CloudTrail event coverage and protect and review resulting logs.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Inappropriate key design or capacity configuration
risks.description: A NoSQL design without validated access patterns can cause unsuitable permissions, inefficient access, or operational failure.
risks.action: Validate partition and sort keys against access patterns, review indexes and capacity, and test recovery settings.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

ec2.name: Amazon EC2
ec2.reason: Amazon EC2 fits the stated need for operating-system control, persistent server processes, or a workload beyond Lambda execution limits.

risks.title: Embedded keys or excessive instance permissions
risks.description: Long-lived credentials or an overprivileged instance profile can expose AWS resources after workload compromise.
risks.action: Use a least-privilege EC2 instance profile and temporary role credentials; remove embedded access keys.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Unnecessary public or administrative ingress
risks.description: Broad security group rules and public placement can expose instance management and application ports.
risks.action: Restrict inbound and outbound rules to required sources and ports and review private subnet or managed access options.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Exposed secrets or unencrypted volumes
risks.description: Plaintext secrets and unreviewed EBS encryption or key permissions can expose application data.
risks.action: Use a suitable secrets-management mechanism, encrypt appropriate EBS volumes, and restrict encryption key permissions.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Missing workload or instance telemetry
risks.description: Uncollected application and operating-system events can conceal failures or suspicious activity.
risks.action: Collect appropriate application and OS logs, review CloudTrail management events, and configure actionable alerts and retention.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Insecure instance defaults or outdated images
risks.description: Unpatched images, weak metadata settings, or unsuitable instance configuration can increase attack exposure.
risks.action: Use reviewed images, establish patching, require IMDSv2 where appropriate, and review launch and recovery configuration.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

lambda.name: AWS Lambda
lambda.reason: AWS Lambda fits the stated event-driven function requirement, subject to current service execution and integration limits.

risks.title: Overprivileged execution or invocation policies
risks.description: Broad execution roles or resource-based invocation policies can grant unintended function or downstream access.
risks.action: Use a dedicated least-privilege execution role and restrict function invocation permissions to trusted principals and sources.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Unreviewed invocation and VPC exposure
risks.description: Public function URLs or unreviewed invocation and VPC paths can expose a function beyond its intended clients.
risks.action: Review function URL authentication and resource policies; restrict VPC security groups only when VPC attachment is needed.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Exposed runtime secrets or sensitive logs
risks.description: Secrets in code or environment configuration and sensitive log content can expose application credentials or data.
risks.action: Use an appropriate secrets service, review environment-variable encryption and access, and avoid logging sensitive values.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Missing function execution visibility
risks.description: Missing logs, metrics, or alarms can leave errors and unexpected invocation patterns unnoticed.
risks.action: Grant only required logging permissions and configure CloudWatch logs, metrics, retention, and relevant alarms.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unsupported runtime or unsuitable execution settings
risks.description: Outdated runtimes or unreviewed timeout, concurrency, and retry settings can cause insecure or unreliable execution.
risks.action: Use a supported runtime, verify execution limits, and review timeout, retry, concurrency, and deployment settings.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

route53.name: Amazon Route 53
route53.reason: Amazon Route 53 provides authoritative DNS management for the stated AWS-managed public domain requirement.

risks.title: Unauthorized DNS administration
risks.description: Broad hosted-zone or record change permissions can redirect website traffic.
risks.action: Restrict Route 53 change permissions to required hosted zones, actions, and administrators.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Unexpected or unowned DNS targets
risks.description: Records pointing at unintended or retired resources can redirect traffic or leave takeover opportunities.
risks.action: Verify DNS target ownership and intended public exposure and remove stale records when resources are retired.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unreviewed DNS integrity protection
risks.description: An unreviewed DNSSEC configuration or sensitive values in records can undermine DNS integrity or expose information.
risks.action: Evaluate DNSSEC signing and delegation where appropriate; avoid credentials or private data in DNS records.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Missing DNS query or change visibility
risks.description: Unavailable query logs and zone-change audit events can delay investigation of unexpected name resolution.
risks.action: Enable appropriate Route 53 query logging and review CloudTrail DNS administration events with suitable retention.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Stale or incorrect DNS records
risks.description: Incorrect aliases, TTLs, delegations, or leftover records can break delivery or reference decommissioned resources.
risks.action: Review hosted-zone delegation, aliases, target ownership, TTLs, and a decommissioning checklist before deployment.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

cloudfront.name: Amazon CloudFront
cloudfront.reason: Amazon CloudFront fits the stated controlled-edge, content delivery, or global caching requirement.

risks.title: Unauthorized distribution changes
risks.description: Broad distribution-management permissions can change origins, certificates, or content delivery behavior.
risks.action: Restrict CloudFront administrative permissions and use reviewed change procedures for distributions and origins.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Direct origin access bypasses the edge
risks.description: A publicly reachable origin can bypass the distribution’s intended access and delivery controls.
risks.action: Restrict origin access; use Origin Access Control for supported S3 origins and appropriate controls for custom origins.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Insecure transport or sensitive content caching
risks.description: Weak viewer or origin transport policies and inappropriate caching can expose data in transit or across users.
risks.action: Require suitable HTTPS viewer and origin policies and exclude private or personalized responses from shared caches as appropriate.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Insufficient edge access visibility
risks.description: Missing access logs or change auditing can hide unusual requests or distribution modifications.
risks.action: Select appropriate standard or real-time logs, protect log destinations, and review CloudTrail changes and useful metrics.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Incorrect cache or certificate configuration
risks.description: Unreviewed cache keys, forwarding policies, origins, or certificates can cause data leakage or delivery failures.
risks.action: Review cache behaviors and cache keys, origins, alternate domains, and ACM certificate region requirements for CloudFront.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

iam.name: AWS IAM
iam.reason: AWS IAM provides identity, role, and permission management for the stated human or workload access requirement.

risks.title: Excessive privileges or weak human authentication
risks.description: Broad policies, weak human authentication, and shared administrator credentials can enable unauthorized AWS access.
risks.action: Prefer federation and temporary credentials, enforce appropriate MFA for humans, protect root access, and apply least privilege.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Overly broad trust and access context
risks.description: Unreviewed role trust and access conditions can permit unintended principals or administrative access paths.
risks.action: Review trusted principals, role assumptions, and appropriate source or organization conditions without creating brittle policy assumptions.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Exposed long-lived credentials
risks.description: Unprotected access keys and broadly accessible secrets can expose AWS resources and stored information.
risks.action: Use temporary credentials where possible, remove unused keys, and protect and rotate unavoidable long-lived credentials.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Insufficient identity activity audit
risks.description: Missing audit coverage can conceal policy changes, unexpected role assumptions, or credential use.
risks.action: Record and review relevant CloudTrail identity and management events and alert on significant privilege changes.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unreviewed IAM policy and role configuration
risks.description: Wildcard policies, stale roles, and unintended trust relationships can persist into deployment.
risks.action: Review permission and trust policies, validate them with available IAM tools, and remove unused identities and permissions.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

acm.name: AWS Certificate Manager
acm.reason: AWS Certificate Manager fits the stated need to manage HTTPS certificates for an integrated AWS endpoint; endpoint and certificate-region requirements must be verified.

risks.title: Unauthorized certificate administration
risks.description: Broad ACM permissions can permit unintended certificate requests, deletion, or changes affecting website TLS.
risks.action: Restrict certificate request, import, export, deletion, and tagging permissions to authorized roles and intended resources.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Unreviewed certificate endpoint integration
risks.description: A certificate without correct endpoint integration does not establish the intended network transport boundary.
risks.action: Verify the supported integrated service, domain coverage, listener or distribution association, and relevant endpoint access controls.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unprotected certificate material or unsuitable TLS use
risks.description: Improper handling of imported or exportable private keys and unreviewed TLS integration can expose credentials or traffic.
risks.action: Prefer managed integrated use where appropriate, protect any private key material, and configure the endpoint to use suitable TLS policies.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unnoticed validation or renewal failures
risks.description: Without monitoring certificate state and renewal prerequisites, a website certificate can expire or fail validation.
risks.action: Monitor certificate status and expiration, retain required validation records, and investigate renewal or validation failures.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Incorrect region, validation, or lifecycle configuration
risks.description: Wrong certificate region, domain validation, or renewal prerequisites can prevent secure endpoint operation.
risks.action: Verify endpoint-specific region requirements, domain validation, certificate association, and managed-renewal eligibility.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

security_groups.name: Security Groups
security_groups.reason: Security Groups provide a stateful network boundary for the stated VPC-attached workload requirement.

risks.title: Unauthorized security group changes
risks.description: Broad permissions to modify security groups can reopen restricted network paths.
risks.action: Restrict security group creation and rule-change permissions and use authorized, reviewed administration roles.

frameworks.reference: Identity and access management (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

risks.title: Unnecessary inbound or outbound access
risks.description: Broad sources, destinations, ports, or protocols can expose VPC-attached resources to unintended traffic.
risks.action: Allow only required traffic; restrict administrative access, prefer appropriate security group references, and review egress needs.

frameworks.reference: Network access controls (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Assuming network rules encrypt application traffic
risks.description: Security Groups filter traffic but do not encrypt it or replace application authentication and secure protocols.
risks.action: Require suitable encrypted application protocols and authentication in addition to restricted security group traffic.

frameworks.reference: SEC08 / SEC09 — Protecting data at rest and in transit
Data protection and encryption (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Missing boundary-change and traffic visibility
risks.description: Unreviewed rule changes and traffic metadata can leave broad access or suspicious paths unnoticed.
risks.action: Review security group changes in CloudTrail and use appropriate VPC Flow Logs and alerts for relevant traffic patterns.

frameworks.reference: Logging and monitoring (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)

risks.title: Unused, stale, or default group rules
risks.description: Unreviewed default groups, obsolete rules, and stale references can retain access after design changes or decommissioning.
risks.action: Review attached groups, default rules, stale references, and unused rules before deployment and resource retirement.

frameworks.reference: Secure configuration and review (thematic; verify the adopted benchmark edition)
